examples.trans: This man is waiting for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы его самого не выиграли?
examples.trans: Did you not win him too?

examples.text: Нет, лучше я скажу сама.
examples.trans: No, it is better if I tell him myself.

examples.text: А ты сама как думаешь?
examples.trans: And what do you think yourself?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Настя, ты телефон дома забыла.
examples.trans: Nastya, you forgot your phone at home.

examples.text: Она сегодня же об этом узнает.
examples.trans: She will find out about this today.

examples.text: Ей уже обо всём донесли.
examples.trans: Someone has already reported everything to her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Тебя сегодня ждёт большое повышение.
examples.trans: A big promotion awaits you today.

examples.text: Она сегодня же об этом узнает.
examples.trans: She will find out about this today.

examples.text: Послушайте, сегодня всё за наш счёт.
examples.trans: Listen, everything is on the house today.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да ладно, не может быть!
examples.trans: Come on, that cannot be!

examples.text: Всё, ладно, мне уже пора.
examples.trans: Alright, that is all, I have to go.

examples.text: Мы предлагаем тебе стать совладельцем ресторана.
examples.trans: We are offering you to become co-owner of the restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе большое, дорогой.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, my dear.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе большое, мой дорогой.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, my dear.

examples.text: Ладно, спасибо тебе за всё.
examples.trans: Alright, thank you for everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вижу, что ты связан с едой.
examples.trans: I see that you are connected with food.

examples.text: Да ты мне в глаза посмотри.
examples.trans: Just look into my eyes.

examples.text: Мне ещё в магазин надо забежать.
examples.trans: I still need to stop by the store.
